name: Rocket Money
tagline: Analyze user-imported transactions and maintain a manual subscription cancellation checklist

pricing.notes: Premium uses a variable user-selected price or package; canonical amount is null.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Rocket Money, analyze user-imported transactions and maintain a manual subscription cancellation checklist. The hard boundary is bank aggregation, bill negotiation, cancellation operations, and financial partnerships, plus financial integrations, compliance, and trust.
coreLoopDIY: Import transactions, categorize them with transparent rules, maintain a manual subscription cancellation checklist, reconcile balances, and export clean reports without moving money.
requirements: CSV or OFX exports from financial institutions
whatYouLose: bank aggregation, bill negotiation, cancellation operations, and financial partnerships
replacementScope: personal ledger or simple invoicing tool
ongoingBurden: import normalization, reconciliation, rule drift, exchange rates, backups, audit trails, tax changes, bank APIs, and support
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Rocket Money because people pay because accurate money records and dependable institution connections are worth more than the visible charts. The recurring cost buys import normalization, reconciliation, rule drift, exchange rates, backups, audit trails, tax changes, bank APIs, and support, not just the visible interface.

prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Rocket Money in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, SQLite, Drizzle ORM, and local-first encryption; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: import transactions, categorize them with transparent rules, maintain a manual subscription cancellation checklist, reconcile balances, and export clean reports without moving money.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Support CSV and OFX import with saved column mappings and duplicate detection.
Implement accounts, transactions, transfers, categories, payees, notes, and split transactions.
Add deterministic categorization rules whose matches can be inspected and undone.
Provide reconciliation, monthly budget, cash-flow, net-worth, and export views.
Keep an immutable import log and require explicit confirmation before destructive changes.
Encrypt local data, create automatic backups, and document restore on a fresh machine.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out initiating payments or moving money.
Deliberately leave out tax, payroll, or accounting compliance guarantees.
Deliberately leave out screen-scraped bank access and commercial institution aggregation.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
